clue.text: Lowly dwellings without hot fires

definitions.note: a verb: dismisses from a job

indicators.note: without tells us to remove a letter from the dwellings word

parts.note: shacks are humble, rough dwellings
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Poor huts that have no warm hearths burning in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fires' looks like part of the heating picture but is the definition, a verb meaning dismisses.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal verbs for dismissing someone from employment.

clue.text: Sailor tucked into special rations in part of ship

indicators.note: tucked into says the sailor word is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: board means meals or food provided
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman eating extra provisions in one part of the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' reads as eating, but it is the container signal; TAR is an old word for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The right-hand side of a vessel, facing forward, is a named section of a ship.

clue.text: Snack served up in Dieppe perchance

indicators.note: served up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A light bite brought to the table in a French port, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'served up' reads the letters from bottom to top: EPERC inside 'Dieppe perchance' becomes CREPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin pancake, often eaten as a light meal or street food, is a snack.

clue.text: Top cricketer facing delivery of several balls

parts.note: a slip is a fielder positioned beside the wicketkeeper in cricket
an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket

explanation.surface: A leading cricketer about to face a set of bowled balls.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a slip is a close fielder and an over is six balls from one bowler. 'Top' reads as 'best' but is the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless pullover sweater is an item of clothing worn on the upper body, a top.

clue.text: Piano works popular with German artist

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft
OPS is short for opuses, musical works
IN means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Keyboard pieces that are well liked, together with a German performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A recording artist is a performer, and a chart vocalist is one example of such an artist.

clue.text: Shrub, say, mostly seen in plot

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a shrub is an example of a plant

explanation.surface: A bush seen in a garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a garden bed but is the scheme sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a scheme or design for doing something, just as a strategy is.

clue.text: Fans, one notes, regularly supporting rugby player

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting pieces sit below the rugby player

parts.note: a prop is a forward in the front row of a rugby scrum
taken as written

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Supporters, one says, regularly back a rugby forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes N, T, S from 'notes'; 'supporting' places ONE NTS under PROP in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Advocates or backers of a cause are its supporters, as fans are.

clue.text: Definitely something done at home

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
a deed is an act, something done

explanation.surface: A chore that was certainly carried out around the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic adverbs of certainty, like 'truly' or 'certainly'.

clue.text: Plum joke penned by English writer

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed, so the joke sits inside the writer's name

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A wisecrack about fruit written by an English author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' looks like authorship but means enclosed; the writer is the novelist Graham Greene.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a variety of plum with green skin, so an example of the fruit.

clue.text: Was inactive, it would seem, in wild west show

definitions.meaning: split as ..., it means rode nothing, so the joke is that no riding happened
an American cowboy show of riding and roping

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical: RODE O read as 'rode zero', i.e. took no rides. 'It would seem' marks this as a playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy contest of bronco riding and roping is a classic Western spectacle.

clue.text: Aboard steamer I can order filter coffee

indicators.note: aboard says the letters are carried within the words that follow, as passengers on a ship

explanation.surface: A passenger on a steamboat decides to order a cup of filter coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aboard' fits the steamer picture but signals that the answer sits inside 'steamer I can order'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an espresso diluted with hot water, a style of coffee resembling the filtered kind.

clue.text: Rastafarian briefly attracted publicity

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: drew means attracted, as a crowd is drawn
AD, short for advertisement, is publicity

explanation.surface: A Rastafarian who got a short burst of media attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' seems to describe the publicity but trims DREW to DRE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jamaican usage a dread is a Rastafarian, named after the dreadlocks members wear.

clue.text: French/British school

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A school that is both French and British.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is the well-known boarding school near Windsor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Brittany is French, so the Brittany native or language counts as French.

clue.text: Inherit small business, revamped on time

parts.note: CO is the short form of company, a business

indicators.note: revamped means remade, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A small firm overhauled and delivering punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revamped' rearranges ON TIME into MEINTO.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into money or property is the idiom for receiving it as a legacy.

clue.text: Affection that comes with some emails?

definitions.meaning: a file sent along with an email

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an emotional bond of fondness and a file added to an electronic message.

clue.text: Wall heater adapted for hot and cold conditions?

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, describing something usable in any climate

indicators.note: adapted means altered to suit, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wall-mounted heater modified to cope with both warm and chilly spells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' reorders the letters of WALL HEATER; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suitable in every kind of climate, such as a pitch or tyre, is described this way.

clue.text: Dodgy US politician, note, with luxury car

parts.note: a log is a written note or record
Roller is British slang for a Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: A shady American politician jotting something down beside his expensive car.
explanation.walkthrough: In US politics logrolling is trading votes or favours between legislators.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who trades votes for mutual advantage is a disreputable kind of American legislator.

clue.text: Installed in home, I settled

indicators.note: installed in says the I is placed inside the word for home

parts.note: a pad is informal for one's flat or home

explanation.surface: Having moved into a house, someone says they've paid up.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that has been settled has been paid off in full.

clue.text: Ailing president's no time for chemist, perhaps

indicators.note: ailing means unwell, so the letters are disordered
no means without, so the time letter is removed

explanation.surface: A sick head of state has no time for the pharmacist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no time' removes T from PRESIDENTS, and 'Ailing' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist hands out medicines, so a chemist is an example of someone who supplies them.

clue.text: Customer finally got free woolly jumper

indicators.note: woolly means vague and muddled, so the letters are jumbled
finally takes the last letter of the word customer

explanation.surface: A shopper ended up with a free knitted sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly' and 'jumper' suggest a sweater (British 'jumper'), but the jumper is a leaping amphibian. 'woolly' jumbles R with GOT FREE.
explanation.definitionFit: This amphibian leaps from branch to branch, so it is literally a creature that jumps.

clue.text: Really likes temporary accommodation

definitions.meaning: slang verb: enjoys or appreciates greatly
lodgings, often rented rooms for students

explanation.surface: Someone is keen on short-term lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang verb means appreciates, and the British noun means rented lodgings.

clue.text: Drinks ultimately stored (except for wine) in cupboards

indicators.note: in places the shortened stored inside the pantries word

parts.note: larders are food cupboards or pantries

indicators.note: except for means the wine is taken away from the word stored

parts.note: red is wine

explanation.surface: The drinks have finally been put away in the cupboards, apart from the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except for' removes the wine from 'stored'. 'Last orders' is the British pub call for final drinks before closing.
explanation.definitionFit: The final round of drink requests before a pub closes is the last drinks of the night.

clue.text: Church with no end of incense for convert

indicators.note: no end of means the last letter is removed

parts.note: to incense is to enrage or anger

explanation.surface: A church without the smell of burning incense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incense' reads as the fragrant smoke but is the verb meaning to enrage.
explanation.definitionFit: To convert something is to transform it, a synonym of altering it.

clue.text: Maybe storm in a teacup created by tea, you say? That's funny

indicators.note: you say tells us the word is spoken, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: a brew is a pot or cup of tea
ha ha is the sound of laughter at something funny

explanation.surface: A tea-related fuss described in someone's chatty way, with a laugh at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: BROU is pronounced like BREW.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm in a teacup is a fuss over nothing, an example of a commotion or uproar.

clue.text: Simple degree is set up by college

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is raised, read upwards

explanation.surface: An undemanding qualification established by a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean elementary, fundamental and uncomplicated.

clue.text: Volkswagen, black one, found in here

indicators.note: found in says the pieces are placed within the word here

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as in pencil grades
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dark car, one of a kind, discovered on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Herbie is the Volkswagen Beetle star of Disney's Love Bug films.
explanation.definitionFit: The film car Herbie is a particular Volkswagen Beetle, so a named example of the make.

clue.text: Short-lived responsibility

definitions.meaning: a remit or set of instructions given to someone

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for fleeting and a noun for one's assigned remit or duties.

clue.text: Feeble joke, ultimately unfunny

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of unfunny

explanation.surface: A weak gag that is, in the end, not funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean weak and lacking in strength.

clue.text: In old hospital, large round room for guests

indicators.note: in places the size and circle letters inside the old hospital word

parts.note: san is a dated short form of sanatorium
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A spacious circular reception room inside a former hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing room or reception room where a host receives visitors is this kind of room.

clue.text: On-line questions about royal palace staff?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the questions word goes round the royal letter

parts.note: e-queries are questions sent electronically
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: Internet enquiries concerning the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but places R inside EQUERIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Officers attending members of the royal household are among the staff of a palace.

clue.text: Far from straight to withhold payment for accommodation these days

indicators.note: to withhold means to hold something back inside, so one word is kept within the other

parts.note: curly hair or lines are far from straight
rent is paid for accommodation

explanation.surface: A crooked tenant holding back rent money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far from straight' suggests dishonesty but just means CURLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean at present, nowadays.

clue.text: Prefer to attack

definitions.meaning: colloquially, to choose or favour something

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to choose an option and to set about assaulting someone.
